name: Jemuel
overview: Jemuel was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, identified as one of the sons of Simeon. He is specifically noted as a son of Simeon who journeyed to Egypt with the family of Israel. His mention is found in the genealogical record of those who went to Egypt, highlighting his place within the Israelite lineage.
namesAndTitles: The individual is known primarily by the name Jemuel, with an alternate form Nemuel appearing in the records. Neither name has a specified meaning provided in the biblical text, and neither is indicated as a name given directly by God. Thus, the names serve mainly as identifiers within the genealogical listings.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jemuel as a son of Simeon, placing him within the family of one of Israel's twelve tribes. Beyond this direct filial relationship, no additional family connections are documented in the biblical text concerning Jemuel.
scriptureSignificance: Jemuel's significance lies in his inclusion among the sons of Simeon who accompanied Israel's family to Egypt, a foundational event in the history of God's people. His mention contributes to the biblical genealogy that traces the descendants of Israel, underscoring God's providential preservation of the chosen family through generations. While not associated with specific deeds or narratives, Jemuel's presence in the record affirms the faithfulness of God's promises to the patriarchs' lineage.
